title: Focal loss (Lin et al. 2017), gamma 1, on the pretraining next-token and MTP cross-entropy: each proof token's CE is weighted by (1 - p_target), logged losses stay plain CE, on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,557,760 params, model unchanged)
description: Idea ID: P47/P48 family (a confidence penalty on the same supervised positions and vocabulary; focal loss itself is not in the backlog and has not run under any protocol here). The gradient of every pretraining CE term (main next-token and the 0.3-weighted MTP term) is reweighted per token by (1 - p_target)^1, so tokens the model already predicts with p ~ 0.99 (formula copies, syntax) stop driving the update and the uncertain tokens (which rule, which named facts to cite, where a proof branches) dominate the gradient direction; the handed-off weights, RL and sampling are unchanged and the recorded train/val losses are still the plain CE means. Expert iteration's round-1 harvest on 7+-line targets is decided by those uncertain decision tokens at T = 0.8, and Mukhoti et al. (2020) show focal training yields calibrated, less overconfident predictors, so the sampler should spend its 64 attempts on the model's genuinely plausible alternatives instead of a collapsed mode, raising targets solved per round without the uniform-over-vocabulary noise that label smoothing (P47) would add.
hypothesis: (1) At 153's final train CE ~0.055 the great majority of proof tokens sit at p > 0.95 and still supply a consistent (1 - p) ~ 0.01-0.05 gradient each; under plain CE they are pushed toward p -> 1 for the whole 4-epoch run, which is where 148/153's late val-loss rise (overfitting the 155k cap-6 records) and an overconfident T = 0.8 sampler come from. Focal weighting (1 - p) makes the push on a p = 0.99 token ~50x smaller than CE's while leaving a p = 0.5 token at half weight and a p ~ 0 token untouched, so the update direction is set by the decision tokens; under Muon (orthogonalised, RMS-matched updates) the overall gradient scale is irrelevant and only this direction change reaches the hidden matrices, while the AdamW group (embeddings, LayerNorms, biases) sees the reweighting fully. (2) Downstream: a model whose confidence tracks its actual uncertainty samples more distinct plausible continuations per target at T = 0.8, so pass@64 on 7+-line targets (round-1 targets solved) rises or holds while per-sample accuracy may fall; 129-claude showed a worse sampler can still win when expert iteration climbs faster, and the RL fine-tune's hard-target CE re-sharpens the easy tokens on the harvested proofs. (3) The main risk is the easy-token plateau: copy/syntax tokens left at p ~ 0.98-0.99 instead of 0.999 compound over ~150-token proofs into more Lean parse failures and nd_verify rejects, lowering round-1 sample accuracy enough that fewer targets are solved (161-fable3's collapse pattern: round-1 targets 353 vs 736 cost 63). Gamma 1 rather than the canonical 2 is chosen to keep that plateau mild. (4) Secondary risk: Muon's orthogonalisation re-amplifies the small consistent easy-token directions, so the effective change is smaller than the loss suggests and the result is rerun noise (160-claude measured -14 for an unchanged model).
expected_delta: -45 to +35 theorems at >= 7 (3-seed mean), central +3; keep needs > 687.00 (153-claude: 676/700/685). Mechanism predictions: n_params 9,557,760 exactly; pretraining steps 4,350-4,700 per seed (153: 4,540/4,479/4,489; no new per-step cost beyond three elementwise ops, +-8% pod spread), epochs 3.8-4.2; peak memory 7.3-7.8 GB. Because focal stops pushing easy tokens to p -> 1, the LOGGED plain-CE train loss should sit ABOVE 153's from ~60 s on: final train CE 0.062-0.095 (153: 0.054-0.060), final val CE 0.085-0.110 (153: 0.088/0.087/0.089) with a shallower late rise (val at 300 s minus its minimum <= 153's ~0.010-0.015); held-out greedy after pretraining 0.945-0.975 (153: 0.9675; argmax is calibration-insensitive, so at most a small drop). RL: round-1 sample accuracy 0.19-0.29 (153: 0.271/0.28/0.21), round-1 targets solved 660-850 (153: 766/747/694), round-4 RL-solved 1,120-1,230 (153: 1,157/1,168/1,191), eval/round-4 ratio 0.56-0.61; RL sampling 190-270 samples/s (model identical); totals 1,600-1,900 s. Falsifiers: (a) final logged train CE <= 0.060 on every seed means Muon neutralised the reweighting (hypothesis 4) and any metric move is noise; (b) round-1 targets solved below 153's on every seed together with a whole-run Lean parse-failure rate above 153's means the easy-token plateau (risk 3) dominated and calibration did not buy diversity; (c) steps < 4,200 on every seed means an unexpected cost. Keep only if the 3-seed mean beats 687; if it wins with round-1 targets solved at or above 153's and a flatter val curve, the calibration mechanism is supported and gamma 2 is the follow-up; if it wins only via faster r1 -> r4 climbing with a worse sampler, it is the 129 plasticity story, not calibration.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude except width; PeriLNBlock now replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280 (same as 151's 4*320)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: none vs 153-claude: the model, its init, the MTP module, the token-budget batches and both optimizers are byte-identical; only the training objective's per-token weighting changes (see loss). n_params 9,557,760 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107)
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same; per Peri-LN block 1,579,136 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 492,800 + fc2 491,904 + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 1,875,584; pretraining trains 11,433,344 in total, so unlike 151 the total is over 10M if the discarded MTP module were counted; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: per-token next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions as in the fork's loss_on, but for the GRADIENT each token's CE is focal-weighted (Lin et al. 2017): focal(ce) = (1 - exp(-ce))^FOCAL_GAMMA * ce = (1 - p_target)^gamma * CE, gamma = 1.0, masked mean over proof tokens (m[:, 1:]). The recorded train_loss/last_loss and val_loss are the PLAIN CE means over the same positions (val_loss still calls the fork's loss_on), so the curve stays comparable with 153
loss.mtp: unchanged DeepSeek-V3-style depth-1 MTP module (z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))), one Peri-LN causal block with the ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2, the model's ln_f/head predicts x_{t+2}); its per-token CE gets the same focal weighting for the gradient, masked mean over m[:, 2:]; the logged mtp_loss is its plain CE mean
loss.total: focal-weighted main + MTP_WEIGHT (0.3, constant) * focal-weighted mtp; both terms are focal so their relative weight stays the same as under plain CE (focal shrinks a term by the mean (1 - p) of its tokens). The modulating factor is not detached (standard focal loss; gradient of -(1-p) log p w.r.t. the target logit is ~2 (1-p)^2 p for p near 1 instead of CE's (1-p), i.e. ~50x smaller at p = 0.99, 5x smaller at p = 0.9, and equal to CE as p -> 0)
loss.focal_reference: Lin, Goyal, Girshick, He, Dollar (2017), Focal loss for dense object detection; Mukhoti et al. (2020), Calibrating deep neural networks using focal loss (focal loss upper-bounds KL(q||p) - gamma * H(p), i.e. a sample-dependent entropy regulariser)
loss.leakage_check: MTP path unchanged from 153 (its CPU leakage check still applies)
loss.local_check: CPU check with fork 51604b3, width-384 model, random tokens (4 x 40, proof mask from position 15): total 6.109 <= main 4.721 + 0.3 * aux 4.814 (focal <= plain CE), backward finite (grad norm 5.82); focal([0.01, 0.1, 0.7, 3.0]) = [0.0001, 0.0095, 0.352, 2.851] with 1 - p = [0.01, 0.095, 0.503, 0.950]; n_params 9,557,760

config.bench: not run: vs 153 the step adds three elementwise ops (exp, sub, pow at gamma 1) on the two ~18k-element per-token CE vectors; model, batches, Muon/AdamW and the val pass are unchanged, so the 153 probe (11.53 steps/s, 7.42 GB, 179 samples/s) stands
